books.title: How to Be a Public Scholar
books.tagline: An accessible, step-by-step guide for scholars seeking to broaden the public impact of their research, writing, and work
books.description:
Many scholars want to engage audiences outside the ivory tower—whether to influence policy, engage communities, share their work through media outlets, build audiences, or counter misinformation. But graduate training often doesn’t teach them the skills they need. Betty S. Lai fills this void by showing scholars how to plan, build, and scale the reach of their research. Drawing on interviews with seventy-five public scholars and media experts, she shares actionable strategies backed by real-world examples. Whether your aim is media interviews, op-eds, social media, book launches, newsletters, or podcasts, How to Be a Public Scholar will help you expand the reach of your ideas while honoring scholarly values of knowledge and responsibility.

Guiding readers each step of the way, Lai explains how to weigh the various options for public scholarship, assess the benefits and drawbacks of different platforms, and formulate a plan for reaching and engaging audiences that makes the most sense for you and your goals. She discusses how to find opportunities, make new connections, develop content, and grow one’s audience. She also provides guidance on how to broaden the reach of your public scholarship work and sustain it while navigating the challenges of publicly engaged work. Along the way, Lai highlights the personal and professional value of doing public-facing work and tackles common questions about self-promotion, time management, the perils of the public sphere, and much more.

Focusing on general strategies that translate across platforms, How to Be a Public Scholar features hands-on exercises, checklists that guide readers through each topic, a launch plan example, a glossary of key terms, and suggestions for further reading.
books.bio: Betty S. Lai is professor of counseling psychology at Boston College and the author of The Grant Writing Guide: A Road Map for Scholars (Princeton). Her research on children and disasters has been recognized with awards from the Society of Counseling Psychology and the American Educational Research Association.

books.title: Jewelry in Portraits of The Frick Collection
books.tagline: Explores some of the precious objects shown in Frick portraits across the early modern period
books.description:
The Frick Collection is renowned for its exquisite paintings, in particular its portraits by European Old Masters. Beyond their captivating sitters, many of these depict a myriad of jewels and other precious items, from diamond necklaces, brooches, and earrings to gold watches, rings, and pearl-studded crowns. While the history of the commissioning, collecting, and significance of these paintings has produced a plethora of valuable scholarship, the jewellery they represent has drawn little to no attention in the literature.

Focusing on a select number of masterpieces across the early modern period, from Jan Van Eyck, William Hogarth, to Jacques-Louis David, this book seeks to shine a light on some of the precious objects shown in Frick portraits. New research drawing from archival sources and recent study allows the legacies of these objects to emerge, together with the lives of the people attached to them.
books.bio: Geoffrey Ripert was The Frick Collection’s 2024–25 Anne Poulet Curatorial Fellow. He is Head of Collections at the Domaine de Dampierre-en-Yvelines, near Paris. He has degrees in the History of Art at the Sorbonne, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the École du Louvre and the Bard Graduate Centre.

books.title: Living the Language of Life
books.subtitle: Tales of Alazor and The Governor
books.tagline: The first English translation of an outstanding modern Italian writer whose delightful stories combine elements of the fairy tale, the philosophical tale, fantasy, and science fiction
books.description:
Twentieth-century Italian writer Rinaldo De Benedetti was a popular science journalist, but he also wrote two remarkable volumes of fiction— Tales of Alazor and The Governor . In Living the Language of Life , acclaimed translator Leah Janeczko presents both books in English for the first time.

Tales of Alazor is a collection of stories and verses about a 99-year-old linguist who sets out to speak with all the things of creation—flora, fauna, people, the elements, even magical creatures. The Governor is a novella in which the immortal, omnipotent ruler of our galaxy visits Earth in human form to observe the anomaly that is mankind and determine its fate. Strikingly different yet equally entertaining, these narratives explore the pleasures and perils of venturing into the world to embrace the human experience.

Filled with gentle humor, philosophy, and compassion, Living the Language of Life offers an ideal introduction to a gifted and unique modern writer.
books.bio: Rinaldo De Benedetti (1903–1996) was a Jewish-Italian journalist and popular science writer who also published poetry and fiction. Leah Janeczko is an Italian-to-English literary translator whose work includes Veronica Raimo’s Lost on Me , which was longlisted for the International Booker Prize, Roberto Piumini’s Glowrushes , and Rosella Postorino’s At the Wolf’s Table/The Women at Hitler’s Table. Ephraim Nissan teaches at Goldsmiths, University of London, and has published on De Benedetti.

books.title: Monetary Economics and Policy
books.subtitle: A Foundation for Modern Currency Systems
books.tagline: A unified framework for understanding monetary policy, including recent unprecedented interventions by central banks
books.description:
Over the past two decades, monetary policy has been deployed in unprecedented ways, as central banks attempted to mitigate the adverse consequences of the 2007–2008 financial crisis, the COVID-19 global lockdown, and recent inflationary surges. In Monetary Economics and Policy , Pierpaolo Benigno offers a new way to understand the potency and effectiveness of monetary policy, presenting a unified modeling framework to analyze policy challenges posed by both paper and digital currency systems. He investigates current theoretical and policy controversies, drawing connections with historical themes in monetary economics.

Benigno examines how central banks control the value of their currency amid competition from cryptocurrencies and private money-like securities; discusses the desirability of inflation targeting for macroeconomic stabilization; and explores theoretical grounds for the unconventional monetary policies seen in the recent period of zero nominal interest rates, including forward guidance, quantitative and credit easing, and helicopter money. He accompanies his analysis with an innovative visual representation of the New Keynesian model and inflation-targeting policies.

Benigno’s novel framework also allows the study of monetary policy normalization through quantitative tightening toward what has become the “new normal.” He discusses the optimal provision of liquidity and the different roles of the government and financial intermediaries. Finally, he recounts historical controversies regarding the inflation-unemployment trade-off to understand the 2020s inflationary surge and delves into the causes and dynamics of hyperinflations, tracing them to the subtle, ambiguous linkages between monetary and fiscal policy and weak balance-sheet conditions for the central bank.
books.bio: Pierpaolo Benigno holds the Chair of Monetary Macroeconomics at the Institute of Economics of the University of Bern, where he is deputy head of the Department of Economics.

praise.q: An advanced presentation of monetary economics and fiscal policy's effect on monetary policy.
praise.by: Choice

praise.q: This book fills a clear void in the existing literature about monetary economics. I am not aware of an existing work that can engage students of monetary economics while unraveling the mysteries of monetary theory. Deep thoughts about the nature of money are clearly presented early and drawn upon to analyze conventional and unconventional monetary policy, crisis management, and inflation. The presentation is rigorous and self-contained.
praise.by: Behzad Diba, Georgetown University

praise.q: Pierpaolo Benigno’s book provides a rigorous framework for understanding how central banks manage to implement their price stability mandates. This is shown to require an appropriate design of monetary policy, with a purposeful use of the different instruments available, including interest rates on reserves, asset purchases, and remittances to the treasury. This monograph is a must-read for those who wish to deepen their knowledge of the theoretical foundations underlying the science of monetary policy.
praise.by: Jordi Galí, author of Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle
praise.cred: author of Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle

praise.q: In the years since the Global Financial Crisis, a stream of unexpected developments has upended earlier paradigms of monetary theory and policy. Among other changes, central bank balance sheets expanded dramatically, government debts reached levels previously seen only after major wars, digital monies including cryptocurrencies emerged, and inflation, once thought to be firmly under control, surged across the world. Pierpaolo Benigno’s book offers a masterful update and synthesis of post-crisis monetary economics. It will be required reading for anyone hoping to understand the evolving role of money.
praise.by: Maurice Obstfeld, University of California, Berkeley

books.title: Poisoning the Well
books.subtitle: How Forever Chemicals Contaminated America
books.tagline: The shocking story of how PFAS, the “forever chemicals” found in everyday household products, poisoned an entire nation
books.description:
Poisoning the Well draws on original, shoe-leather reporting in four highly contaminated towns and damning documents from the polluters’ own files to trace an ugly history of corporate greed and devastated human lives.

We learn that PFAS, toxic chemicals found in everything from cooking pans to mascara, are coursing through the veins of 97 percent of Americans. We witness the pain of families who lost sisters and daughters, cousins and neighbors after PFAS leached into their drinking water. We discover evidence that the makers of forever chemicals may have known for decades about the deadly risks of their products—because their own scientists have been documenting these dangers since the 1960s. And we see the failure of our government, time after time, to provide basic protections to its citizens.

It is impossible to read this searing exposé without being infuriated by the recklessness of corporate America. But readers will also be awed by the spirit of ordinary people who, while fighting for their own lives, took it upon themselves to fix a broken regulatory system. Heart-wrenching and maddening, stirring and uplifting, Poisoning the Well offers a unique window into the worst and best of human nature. It is essential reading for anyone concerned about the unfettered power of industry and the invisible threat it poses to the health of the nation—and to each of us.
books.bio: Sharon Udasin is an environment reporter based in Boulder, Colorado, who has been delving into water contamination and conservation issues for years. She was a Ted Scripps Fellow in Environmental Journalism at the University of Colorado Boulder and has reported for The Hill , The Jerusalem Post , and New York Jewish Week . Rachel Frazin is a journalist based in Washington, DC, who covers energy and environment politics and policy. She has reported for The Hill , The Daily Beast , the Chicago Sun-Times , the Tampa Bay Times , and The Palm Beach Post .

praise.q: In this detailed exposé of corporate evasiveness, inadequate governmental response, and determined lawyers and grassroots activists, the authors precisely elucidate environmental and health concerns, landmark court cases, and some hope for technologies that may eventually eradicate these poisons. An eye-opening chronicle of a pervasive chemical disaster that must be more urgently and openly addressed.
praise.by: Booklist (starred review)

praise.q: Poisoning the Well is an important, disturbing, and beautifully crafted exposé. It unmasks the shameless habits of companies and governments that have been kicking the can down the road for decades — promoting chemicals that have not passed the test of science and unleashing them into the taps of an unsuspecting American public.
praise.by: Erin Brockovich, consumer advocate and environmental activist

praise.q: This book takes readers on a journey through the lives of people whose health has been shattered by the toxic grip of forever chemicals. Through real-life stories of pain, loss, and resilience, Poisoning the Well exposes the true cost of poisons that are now everywhere. And it provides a road map for how we can regulate these chemicals and bring justice to frontline communities.
praise.by: Leah Stokes, University of California, Santa Barbara, and author of Short Circuiting Policy
praise.cred: University of California, Santa Barbara, and author of Short Circuiting Policy

praise.q: Poisoning the Well is a riveting portrait of the harm caused by PFAS, the forever chemicals which are present everywhere and in all of us. It clearly demonstrates the need to turn off the tap of production and use of these toxic and ubiquitous chemicals.
praise.by: Linda Birnbaum, former Director of the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences
praise.cred: former Director of the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences

books.title: The Nile Flows with Gold
books.subtitle: Money and the Global Economy of Roman Egypt
books.tagline: How the circulation of coins reflects the movement of people and goods in Roman Egypt
books.description:
In The Nile Flows with Gold , Irene Soto Martín examines ancient Egypt’s economic integration with the Roman world through a numismatic lens. Soto Marín shows that the circulation of coins after the monetary reforms of Diocletian in the third century CE offers a new perspective on broader questions of trade, connectivity, and provincial economic strength in Roman Egypt. When Egypt entered the imperial monetary zone, it was a monumental change for the province—but it also removed a monetary barrier that had separated Egypt from the rest of the Empire. Patterns of circulation, considered with papyrological and archaeological data, show Roman Egypt to be a monetized, economically powerful province able to absorb coinage from all mints around the Empire.

Soto Marín argues that Egypt’s monetary profile offers compelling evidence for a sustained positive balance of trade, demonstrating that the province exported substantially more goods than it imported and occupied a uniquely central position in the Roman economy. She situates these findings within a broader historical context, tracing Egypt’s monetary history from the Pharaonic period through the fourth century CE and describing the evolution of its monetary systems, the demise of silver, and the emergence of gold as the de facto currency of the late Roman world. Egypt’s economic prominence, she contends, was rooted not simply in its role within the Empire but in enduring geographical and commercial advantages that connected the Mediterranean, Africa, and the Near East for millennia.
books.bio: Irene Soto Marín is associate professor of classics at Harvard University. She is the coeditor of Ancient Taxation: The Mechanics of Extraction in Comparative Perspective .
subjects: Economic History & History of Economic Thought

books.title: Writing on the Job (Revised Edition)
books.subtitle: Best Practices for Communicating in the Digital Age
books.tagline: A fully revised edition of the popular guide to writing for professionals, students, and instructors, now with tips for using AI responsibly and effectively
books.description:
Writing is an essential skill in today’s workplace. From messaging platforms and social media to traditional forms of communication like memos and reports, we rely on words more than ever. Writing on the Job is a practical and compact guide to clear and effective writing. This revised edition includes a new chapter on writing with AI as well as an instructional guide and an invaluable writer’s checklist. Writing on the Job shares essential practices that can improve the performance of any individual or organization.

Drawing on her popular writing classes and workshops as well as her decades of experience in the public and private sectors, Martha Coven explains how to develop a professional style, get started on a piece of writing, create a first draft, and edit it into a strong final product. Coven offers practical advice on more than a dozen forms of writing, from emails and slide decks to proposals and cover letters. Along the way, she provides a wealth of concrete examples and simple templates that make concepts easy to understand and apply.
books.bio: Martha B. Coven has taught at Princeton and NYU and is the founder of Coven Consulting LLC, which offers strategic advice, training, and research services to nonprofits and philanthropic organizations. She has been writing on the job for more than thirty years, in the White House, for members of Congress, and in the private sector.

praise.q: Crisp writing and clear examples guide readers through drafting and editing documents, creating résumés, delivering criticism, presenting statistics, constructing slide decks, and even deciding when to use emojis. . . . Compact and readable chapters for all who text, blog, craft memos, and otherwise communicate online.
praise.by: Library Journal

praise.q: Coven condenses over twenty-five years of professional experience into sixteen tight chapters averaging just seven pages. . . . What some books address in chapters Coven covers in paragraphs. Her book works because it’s about core principles: knowing one’s readers; foregrounding their needs; and striving for clarity, brevity, and liveliness. Essential for reaching those aims is embracing the BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front) strategy of the US Department of Defense. Coven BLUFs a lot in Writing on the Job , and the book is all the clearer, crisper, and livelier as a result.
praise.by: Steven E. Gump, Journal of Scholarly Publishing

praise.q: Easy to read and served up in bite-sized chunks, this book is an excellent ‘how to’ manual for clear communication.
praise.by: Terry Freedman, Teach Secondary

praise.q: By tackling real challenges professionals face, Coven offers practical tips that can improve the performance of any organization.
praise.by: Princeton Alumni Weekly

praise.q: Writing clearly and succinctly is an essential skill that is far too rare. Martha Coven’s book offers keen insights and practical guidance for effective communication, no matter the audience or mission. Writing on the Job lays out a commonsense approach to writing with uncommon clarity.
praise.by: Jacob J. Lew, former US Secretary of the Treasury
praise.cred: former US Secretary of the Treasury

praise.q: Coven smartly and concretely gives readers a road map for turning ideas into action in the twenty-first century workplace. Writing on the Job shouldn’t be on your bookshelf—put it on your desk beside your mouse or trackpad for reference, early and often.”—Melody C. Barnes, executive director of the Karsh Institute of Democracy at the University of Virginia, former director of the White House Domestic Policy Council

Every page of this slim volume has a wealth of real-world experience distilled into actionable and sage advice. Note to those early in their careers—do yourself a favor and read this book now and carefully. It will return that modest investment several times over.
praise.by: Ashvin B. Chhabra, author of The Aspirational Investor: Taming the Markets to Achieve Your Life’s Goals
praise.cred: author of The Aspirational Investor: Taming the Markets to Achieve Your Life’s Goals

praise.q: Communicating clearly and confidently is an essential career skill. Writing on the Job is a concise, accessible guide to business writing in today’s workplace.
praise.by: Margaret Steen, UC Berkeley Extension business writing instructor
praise.cred: UC Berkeley Extension business writing instructor

praise.q: Martha Coven delivers a concise, thoughtful book that provides useful learning for a lifetime. She demonstrates how to write with clarity and liveliness, all the while illuminating why it is important for connecting with your audience. Essential for young professionals and seasoned writers alike.
praise.by: Myles C. Thompson, founding publisher of Columbia Business School Publishing
praise.cred: founding publisher of Columbia Business School Publishing

praise.q: Ideas are the lifeblood of enterprise, but they only matter if communicated effectively. In this brief book, Martha Coven exemplifies this lesson by explaining how to write clearly and compellingly across all of today’s forms of communication, from emails and memos to speeches and slide decks. The result is an ‘elements of professional style’ for the twenty-first century.
praise.by: Donald H. Chew, editor of the Journal of Applied Corporate Finance
praise.cred: editor of the Journal of Applied Corporate Finance

books.title: Drawing Apocalypse
books.subtitle: Architecture and the Specter of Nuclear Annihilation
books.tagline: A timely and original study of speculative and imaginary architectural works created in response to nuclear apocalyptic culture in the US during the Cold War and beyond.
books.description:
What does it mean to imagine the future when the future itself is at stake? In Drawing Apocalypse, Eliyahu Keller brings together the work of three visionary architects—Paolo Soleri, Raimund Abraham, and Lebbeus Woods to address this urgent and calamitous question. These architects, who rarely built actual structures, responded to the nuclear age in different ways: through radical visions of cities, poetic meditations on the idea of house, or revolutionary science fiction narratives that challenge the social and political role of architecture. Keller situates their work within a constellation of historical events, strategic policies, cultural currents, and artifacts that defined the nuclear age.

Drawing Apocalypse also explores the nuclear age’s lingering impact on our own contemporary condition and on how we imagine the future. Bringing together architectural history and theory with Cold War history, cultural studies, and philosophy, the author proposes a new way to think about the relationship between architecture and crisis, and draws parallels between the history of nuclear fears, the present climate crisis, and contemporary technological anxieties. As such, it speaks to a global audience of scholars, designers, and cultural readers who are interested in thinking critically about the connection between imagination, architecture, and technology in the face of unprecedented challenges.
books.bio: Eliyahu Keller is Assistant Professor of Architecture and Town Planning at Technion—Israel Institute of Technology.

books.title: Economic Security for All
books.subtitle: The Feminist Case for a Basic Income in the United States
books.tagline: A feminist case for why a basic income should be implemented in the U.S.—and how it can be achieved.
books.description:
Providing economic security for all is the unfinished business of the New Deal and Great Society programs of the 1930s and 1960s. These first two “big bangs” of social policy development were based on the recognition that economic security in a capitalist economy can only result from a combination of earned income, family resources, and income support organized and distributed by the government. But our current social policy programs have been designed with male life patterns in mind, undermining the economic security of women and others with disproportionate responsibility for care. These policy programs impose higher taxes on working mothers, disincentivize women’s employment, penalize marriage for those with low incomes, and reinforce gendered responsibility for paid employment and unpaid care.

Economic Security for All joins feminist research on social policy with a feminist perspective on basic income to propose gender-inclusive reforms to these policy programs. Almaz Zelleke argues that reforms in the direction of an unconditional , universal , and individual basic income are the key to creating gender-inclusive social policy in the U.S., and to accelerating stalled progress toward gender equality in the U.S. and other capitalist economies.

The author lays out a series of steps that individually advance the gender-inclusion of specific policy programs and together describe a modular and incremental pathway to a full basic income, for both the US and beyond.
books.bio: Almaz Zelleke is Professor of Practice Emerita in Political Science at NYU Shanghai. Her research focuses on the intersection of political theory and public policy and on the ethics and implementation of a basic income.

books.title: Feeling with Things
books.subtitle: Toward a Theory of Material Affective Scaffolding
books.tagline: How we use objects and environments to actively shape and regulate our affective experiences.
books.description:
We shape our affective states through more than just our thoughts. Whether it be through a warm bath, a favorite song, carefully dimmed lighting, or a well-chosen outfit, humans routinely manipulate their material surroundings to enhance and transform their affective states—to relax, feel more confident, create a romantic atmosphere, entertain oneself and others, and so on. In this pioneering work, Giovanna Colombetti examines Material Affective Scaffolding (MAS)—the countless ways we use material objects and built environments to support and shape how we feel.

Though these practices are often mundane and easily overlooked, they illuminate a fundamental aspect of human nature—the desire to manipulate our surroundings to modulate our feelings. While scholars have extensively studied the situated and distributed nature of cognition, the affective dimension of the situated mind has been largely neglected until recently. Feeling with Things fills that critical gap, exploring how emotion and affect are not merely embodied but are fundamentally situated within our material world.
books.bio: Giovanna Colombetti is Professor of Philosophy in the Department of Political and Social Sciences, Philosophy and Anthropology at the University of Exeter, and leads the research cluster “Mind, Body, and Culture” within EGENIS–The Centre for the Study of the Life Sciences. She is the author of The Feeling Body (MIT Press).

books.title: How Rabbis Became Experts
books.subtitle: Social Circles and Donor Networks in Jewish Late Antiquity
books.tagline: How rabbinic expertise was socially constructed, performed, and defended in Roman Palestine
books.description:
At the turn of the common era, the Jewish communities of Roman Palestine saw the organization of a small group of literate Jewish men who devoted their lives to the interpretation and teaching of their sacred ancestral texts. In this groundbreaking study, Krista Dalton shows that these early rabbis were not an insular specialist group but embedded in a landscape of Jewish piety. Drawing on the writings of rabbis in Roman Palestine from the second through fifth centuries CE, Dalton illuminates the significance of social relationships in the production of rabbinic expertise. She traces the social interactions—everyday instances of mutual exchange, from dinner parties to tithes and patronages—that fostered the perception of rabbis as experts.

Dalton shows how the knowledge derived from the rabbis’ technical skills was validated and recognized by others. Rabbis socialized and noshed with neighbors and offered advice and legal favors to friends. In exchange for their expert judgments, they received invitations, donations, appointments, and recognition. She argues that their status as Torah experts did not arise by virtue of being scholars but from their ability to persuade others that their mobilization of Jewish cultural resources was beneficial. Dalton describes the relational processes that made rabbinic expertise possible as well as the accompanying tensions; social interactions shaped the rabbis’ domain of knowledge while also imposing expectations of reciprocity that had to be managed. Dalton’s authoritative analysis demonstrates that a focus on friendship and exchange provides a fuller understanding of how rabbis claimed and defended their distinct expertise.
books.bio: Krista N. Dalton is associate professor of religion and Jewish studies at Denison University.

praise.q: Dalton does an excellent job explaining the changes that occurred during this time period and how the ancient rabbis were able to successfully attain the position of expert, even when their rulings were not universally accepted by Jews. Anyone interested in the development of rabbinic Judaism will want to read this work.
praise.by: Rabbi Rachel Esserman, The Reporter Group

praise.q: Dalton has carefully sifted through the evidence and produced a fine study, synthesizing insights from Jewish studies with the contours of Roman history, bringing both into greater relief.
praise.by: Choice

praise.q: How Rabbis Became Experts is a fascinating and intellectually stimulating scholarly masterpiece.
praise.by: Tom Wilson, Reviews in Religion & Theology

praise.q: [Dalton] does historians a great service in rendering the rabbis more legible, using the lens of expertise to redescribe their dynamics with one another and the affinities they bore to diverse contemporaries who, likewise, aspired to text-based authority in a world where illiteracy prevailed. How Rabbis Became Experts joins a handful of recent books that help to close the distance between Rabbinics and other fields of historical inquiry.
praise.by: Heidi Wendt, American Historical Review

praise.q: Bringing textual, historical, and material culture analysis to bear on this significant historical question, Dalton offers a convincing model of how the ancient rabbis achieved positions of social influence.
praise.by: Elizabeth Shanks Alexander, Biblical Archaeology Society

praise.q: This is a compelling, engaging, and well written volume that illuminates an important question: the way the rabbis came to be regarded as experts, and how that expertise developed in social and relational terms. Dalton’s rich and striking account sheds fresh light on one of the most crucial elements of rabbinic culture.
praise.by: Julia Watts Belser, Georgetown University

praise.q: In this engaging book, Dalton challenges the notion that rabbinic expertise was grounded primarily in the mastery of Torah and Jewish law. Without denying the depth and breadth of their learning, Dalton demonstrates that the rabbis achieved expert status primarily through everyday activities of mutual exchange within the social networks of their time and place. This book will help us to rethink the role of knowledge in establishing expertise, not only in the rabbinic world, but also in the early church, and in our own time.
praise.by: Adele Reinhartz, University of Ottawa

praise.q: How Rabbis Became Experts is a revelatory exploration of how rabbis in Roman Palestine gained recognition as experts through everyday social interactions. This thoroughly human account invites readers to rethink the relational dynamics at the heart of ancient Jewish life, and how they were deeply embedded within the larger Roman world. An essential read for anyone interested in Jewish history, religious authority, and the sociology of knowledge.
praise.by: Simcha Gross, University of Pennsylvania

praise.q: The book makes a significant contribution to Jewish studies. The argument is clear, streamlined, convincing, and important. The author’s writing is superb and among the best I have seen in academia for a scholarly monograph. It takes up some topics of research that had been addressed by scholars in the early years of critical scholarship on rabbinics and looks at these topics in fresh light, with new tools.
praise.by: Gregg E. Gardner, University of British Columbia

books.title: If Einstein Had Known
books.subtitle: The Amazing Reality of Entanglement
books.tagline: A groundbreaking work on quantum physics, tracing more than a century of physics history, that explores the questions that have occupied the greatest physicists.
books.description:
If Einstein Had Known is a unique exploration of Alain Aspect’s fascination with the debate between two giants of physics Niels Bohr and Albert Einstein over the interpretation of quantum mechanics. Aspect places this debate within the incredible history of quantum physics. And while his admiration for Einstein is clear, he also shows us how Einstein’s quasi-philosophical controversy with Bohr led to very real experiments, and to the invention of new quantum technologies.

Almost half a century after his own experiments, Aspect was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for demonstrating that indeed it was necessary to abandon Einstein’s vision of the quantum world.

Recounting his career, Aspect explains with passion and clarity how he demonstrated one of the most extraordinary properties of quantum entanglement and tries to imagine Einstein's reaction to his experimental results.
books.bio: Alain Aspect is a French physicist who won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics (with John Clauser & Anton Zeilinger) for his landmark experiments proving that quantum entanglement is real, settling the famous Einstein–Bohr debate and laying groundwork for quantum tech. He is known for testing Bell’s inequalities, showing particles remain connected regardless of distance, and his work also contributed to laser cooling of atoms, making him a pioneer in quantum information science.

books.title: Immersive Encounters with Mars
books.subtitle: Science, Art, and Imagination in Rover Images
books.tagline: A richly illustrated account of how contemporary rover images of Mars are transformed into immersive experiences.
books.description:
How do we see and make sense of a planet we cannot touch? Immersive Encounters with Mars offers a vivid exploration of how contemporary rover images of Mars are made, interpreted, and transformed into experience. Drawing on firsthand accounts from NASA, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and Airbus Defence and Space, Luci Eldridge unveils the scientific, imaginative, and intuitive practices behind the use of panoramas, 3D visualizations, color-balanced and false-color images, rover driving interfaces, and the simulated terrains of Mars Yards.

Interweaving art history, critical image theory, science and technology studies, philosophy, and glitch theory, the book argues that scientific imaging practices are deeply indebted to the long history of immersive art. The scientific examples in this book share with their art historical counterparts a reliance on imaginative projection: the ability to extend perception, inhabit images, and access what lies beyond immediate human experience.

Both analytical and speculative, this book invites readers to step imaginatively into an image of Mars.
books.bio: Luci Eldridge is an artist and Lecturer in Fine Art at Winchester School of Art (University of Southampton), where she leads interdisciplinary education and research projects that engage critically with image practices across the arts and sciences. She codirects a research group exploring the implications of robotic seeing and sensing, and in 2024, coedited the book Robotic Vision and Virtual Interfacings . She is also Arts Editor for the Journal of Cultural Politics.

books.title: Jung's Life and Work
books.subtitle: Interviews for Memories, Dreams, Reflections with Aniela Jaffé
books.authors: C. G. Jung, John Peck, Aniela Jaffé, Sonu Shamdasani, Heather McCartney
books.tagline: The complete interviews that served as the basis for Jung’s bestselling memoir Memories, Dreams, Reflections Features a significant amount of material withheld from the original book Newly translated and thoroughly annotated by world-renowned Jung expert Sonu Shamdasani
books.description:
In 1957, at the age of eighty-one, C. G. Jung began a collaboration with his student and secretary Aniela Jaffé and the legendary publisher Kurt Wolff on a book about his life. Memories, Dreams, Reflections would become a bestseller, yet it draws from less than half of Jaffé’s original interviews with Jung. Much of the material from these candid, wide-ranging conversations was left on the cutting-room floor. Jung’s Life and Work presents these interviews in their entirety for the first time.

Marking the 150th anniversary of Jung’s birth, this new English translation captures the cadence and subtlety of the brilliant psychologist in his own words, giving voice to a thinker and teacher who is by turns witty and intellectually daring but also vulnerable and humbled by the world’s great mysteries. It restores numerous passages that were originally omitted or heavily edited and toned down for publication, “auntified” as Jung himself put it. Taken together, these talks reveal Jung actively discovering meaningful new connections in his life’s work. He shares his impressions of notable figures he encountered throughout his life—such as Sigmund Freud, William James, Albert Einstein, and H. G. Wells—and describes his striking visions, religious and paranormal experiences, and pioneering self-experimentation. Aided by Jaffé’s skillful questioning, Jung reflects on subjects ranging from Christianity and Buddhism and the fate of the West to the experiences that led to the formulation of his signature concepts of the collective unconscious, archetypes, anima and animus, and the shadow as well as on karma, the afterlife, and much more.

With an introduction and extensive annotations by acclaimed Jung scholar Sonu Shamdasani that provide invaluable historical perspective, Jung’s Life and Work includes previously unpublished extracts from Jung’s letters and a completely reorganized text.
books.bio: C. G. Jung (1875–1961) was one of the most important psychologists of the twentieth century and the founder of analytical psychology. Aniela Jaffé (1903–1991) was an analyst and longtime collaborator with Jung. Sonu Shamdasani is Professor of Jung History and Co-Director of the Health Humanities Centre at University College London and the editor of Jung’s Red Book . Thomas Fischer is an editor at the Foundation of the Works of C. G. Jung and a great-grandson of Jung. Heather McCartney is a Jungian analyst and the translator of Analytical Psychology in Exile (Princeton). John Peck is a Jungian analyst and acclaimed poet.

praise.q: Nothing . . . quite prepares one for the oneiric delights to be found in Jung’s Life and Work. . . . A biographical treasure trove, containing heaps of exciting new material.
praise.by: Amelia Butler-Gallie, The Spectator

praise.q: A rare chance to hear Jung unfiltered, these newly translated interviews restore the wit, daring, and mysticism edited out of his famous memoir. . . . Sonu Shamdasani’s meticulous annotations and previously unpublished material deepen the sense of discovery, revealing a mind still probing the mysteries of psyche, religion, and destiny at the end of his life.
praise.by: Indulge Magazine

praise.q: A real treasure trove for Jung enthusiasts. . . . No reader who engages profoundly and existentially with this book will find their own lives unaffected by its insights.
praise.by: David Lorimer, Paradigm Explorer

praise.q: When we read the original protocols of the Jaffé interviews, we hear Jung’s voice at last. Readers everywhere will be delighted by the chance to hear Jung speaking for himself.
praise.by: John Beebe, author of Integrity in Depth

praise.q: This detailed and extensive book bears witness to all the events that led up to the publication of Memories, Dreams, Reflections and shows how the urge for self-inquiry and the autobiographical was formative for the development of Jung’s lifework.
praise.by: Marion Detjen, Bard College Berlin

books.title: Lee Ufan Sculptures
books.subtitle: A Catalogue Raisonné, 1968–2025
books.authors: David Grosz and Christine Shang-Oak Lee
books.tagline: The definitive catalogue of contemporary artist Lee Ufan’s sculptural oeuvre
books.description:
This catalogue raisonné of the acclaimed artist Lee Ufan (b. 1936) is a sweeping and visually arresting record of his groundbreaking sculptural practice. Working with steel and stone—and occasionally glass, cotton, light bulbs, and other locally sourced materials—Lee composes powerful sculptural installations that activate sites of encounter. By juxtaposing these natural and industrial materials in their mostly unaltered states, Lee encourages engagement between the objects, the site of installation, and the viewer.

Collectively titled Relatum , these site-specific installations originated in 1968 with the emergence of Japan’s avant-garde Mono-ha group, of which Lee was a key theoretician and leading practitioner. Along with the artist’s increasingly international presence and renown, they have often grown monumental in scale and been installed in diverse settings—in museums, galleries, private homes, and public spaces, including historical venues like the Château de Versailles and the Palais des Papes in Avignon. Yet across decades, the work has remained remarkably true to his original vision: spare in form, subtle in execution, and profound in meaning.

With more than 960 catalogue entries—each supported by photography, exhibition details, and historical notes—this publication documents six decades of Lee Ufan’s sculptural installations and offers an intimate look at his creative practice through select writings.

As the essential resource on Lee Ufan’s life and work, this catalogue also includes:

An illustrated chronology of Lee’s life featuring archival photography

Scholarly essays on the sculpture’s evolving meaning and the innovative methodology created for the catalogue

Exhibition histories

Bibliographies

An index of concepts that groups installations with the same type of materials in the same configuration, offering a crucial vantage point for tracing the development of the artist’s three-dimensional oeuvre.

Distributed for Cahiers d’Art Institute
books.bio: David Grosz , the former editorial director at Cahiers d’Art Institute and Artifex Press, has collaborated on and published more than a dozen catalogues raisonnés. Christine Shang-Oak Lee is a research director for the Lee Ufan Catalogue Raisonné.

books.title: Not Like Us
books.subtitle: Why AI Isn't as Human as We Think (and Why That's a Good Thing)
books.tagline: A systematic field guide for critically evaluating the differences and similarities between humans and artificial intelligence.
books.description:
In an era oversaturated with AI hype and apocalyptic predictions, Not Like Us offers a clear-eyed, level-headed field guide for making sense of artificial intelligence. Dirk Hovy approaches AI through a distinctly human lens, rejecting both techno-utopianism and doom-mongering to present a refreshingly pragmatic framework: AI models are instruments designed to solve specific problems, not oracles that will reshape society or doom humanity. By celebrating what makes humans fundamentally different from machines, the book explores how humans and AI can complement, rather than compete with one another.

Not Like Us demystifies the uncertainty around AI by explaining what today's systems are, and what they can and cannot do. Through stories drawn from science, history, and everyday technology, the book offers practical questions to evaluate AI critically: What are models genuinely good at? Where do they predictably fail? Who stands to benefit, and who might be disadvantaged? Covering global perspectives, including multilingual AI, universal risks, and diverse regulatory frameworks, Not Like Us gives curious readers a shared vocabulary and a durable mental model to cut through hype, calm fears, and make better decisions about AI as it evolves alongside us.
books.bio: Dirk Hovy is Professor of Computing Sciences at Bocconi University. He has worked on AI and natural language processing since 2007 and has published over 150 papers and two textbooks, Text Analysis in Python for Social Scientists: Prediction and Classification, and Text Analysis in Python for Social Scientists: Discovery and Exploration.

books.title: On Dreams and the East
books.subtitle: Notes of the 1933 Berlin Seminar
books.authors: C. G. Jung, Heinrich Zimmer, Giovanni V. R. Sorge
books.tagline: Jung’s landmark seminar on the symbolism of yoga and its applications to dream analysis
books.description:
In the summer of 1933, C. G. Jung conducted a seminar in Berlin attended by a large audience of some 150 people, including several Jewish Jungians who would soon leave Germany. Hitler had begun consolidating his position as dictator and these students were distressed at Jung’s recent decision to accept the presidency of a German professional psychotherapy society that was rapidly becoming Nazified and purged of Jews. On Dreams and the East makes these seminar sessions widely available for the first time, offering tantalizing insights into Jung’s evolving understanding of yoga and the realization of the self.

The seminar commences with a presentation on the psychology of yoga by noted Indologist and linguist Heinrich Zimmer, whose collaboration in these talks reflects Jung’s growing engagement with the Hindu tradition, particularly Tantric yoga. Jung analyzes a series of dreams of a middle-aged male patient, focusing on mandalas and the centering process. He reflects on related motifs in alchemical symbolism, Navaho healing drawings, Mithraism, baptism symbolism, the foundation of Rome, ecclesiastic dances, and labyrinths, drawing connections with the symbolism of yoga and Tantra.

Featuring a richly documented introduction by Giovanni Sorge, On Dreams and the East opens a window on Jung’s deepening exploration of Eastern thought and the comparative study of the individuation process at a critical juncture in his life and work.
books.bio: C. G. Jung (1875–1961) was one of the most important psychologists of the twentieth century and the founder of analytical psychology. Heinrich Zimmer (1890–1943) was an Indologist, linguist, and historian of South Asian art. His books include The King and the Corpse , Myths and Symbols in Indian Art and Civilization , Philosophies of India , and The Art of Indian Asia (all Princeton). Giovanni V. R. Sorge is an editor at the Philemon Foundation and an independent researcher who has collaborated with the University of Zurich and with ETH Zurich. He specializes in the history of Jungian analytical psychology and of psychoanalysis and has written extensively on Jung.

books.title: On War and Creativity
books.subtitle: How Military Innovation Shapes Conflict
books.tagline: A highly original investigation of the consequential impact of creativity on military innovation and warfare, from the Enlightenment to the present.
books.description:
War is generally associated with death and destruction—not creativity, nor the power to invent and build. But Dan Öberg argues in On War and Creativity , the two have more in common than meets the eye. Informed and shaped by ideas of creativity, this book characterizes war as part of an age-old martial dream of destroying while giving birth to the new and unimaginable. The author reveals, traces, and contextualizes this dream as a historical undercurrent spanning centuries.

To understand the role creativity plays not only in war but also in society, we must take those who wage war seriously. Accordingly, this book focuses on military thinking and practice, tracing war from the Enlightenment battlefields to our present era obsessed with creative destruction and disruptive innovation. In this analysis, military creativity emerges as an undercurrent that enables and empowers those who embody and enact it. The book presents a new perspective on the history of war, showing how creativity, and associated notions such as genius and innovation, play pivotal roles in the waging and understanding of war. Speaking directly to the current debate about the decline in the liberal rules-based order, Öberg reveals how the relationship between war and creativity is shaping an emerging order based on disruptive political ideas.
books.bio: Dan Öberg is Associate Professor of War Studies at the Swedish Defense University and a former visiting professor at the University of Tokyo.

books.title: Roman Leviathan
books.subtitle: Architecture and Capitalism in Postwar Italy
books.tagline: A powerful revision of the architectural history of postwar Italy that shows how a secretive Vatican-backed developer reshaped the skyline of Rome. A bold, visually rich study that reveals how architecture is produced through the infrastructures of real estate, construction, and mass media.
books.description:
A bold, visually rich study that reveals how architecture is produced through the infrastructures of real estate, construction, and mass media.

In the decades after the Second World War, the Società Generale Immobiliare (SGI), a Vatican-backed real estate and construction giant, reshaped the urban development of Rome and other cities across postwar Italy. In Roman Leviathan, Davide Spina details how this secretive company, with strong links to American capital, changed both the skyline of the Eternal City and the profile of Italian architectural practice by putting modern design and construction in the service of profit-making. The book exposes SGI as a decisive political and economic force, operating at the intersection of architecture, real estate, and Cold War geopolitics, while remaining essentially unregulated and unexplored.

Roman Leviathan reconstructs three decades of SGI’s activities (1945–1975), spanning apartment blocks, suburban estates, and luxury hotels. Focusing in turn on politics, professionalism, labor, technology, Americanization, and historiography, Spina shows how the company’s design decisions were not simply aesthetic choices but responses to market forces, and traces how SGI’s projects entered the cultural imagination through cinema, print media, and popular taste. The book integrates political history, economic analysis, and urban studies with close readings of buildings, revealing architecture as the product of complex negotiations between capital and labor and as a vessel for ideology.
books.bio: Davide Spina is Assistant Professor at Hong Kong University, where he teaches the history and theory of architecture. His articles have appeared in Architectural History , AA Files , and Log .

books.title: Smart as a Fish
books.subtitle: The Unseen Intelligence Beneath the Water
books.tagline: An unprecedented journey into the hidden and surprisingly complex world of fish cognition
books.description:
It is easy think of fish as simple, instinct-driven animals. With their tiny brains and seemingly mindless way of drifting through the water, there appears to be nothing going on inside their heads. Smart as a Fish upends this common misperception, revealing how these creatures possess a rich set of cognitive skills finely tuned to the demands of aquatic life, and how the origins of human intelligence may reach further into the evolutionary past than we realize.

Introducing readers to the pioneering scientists conducting behavioral observations and innovative experiments, Tyrone Lucon-Xiccato brings together a growing body of evidence showing that fish engage with the world in ways that are surprisingly similar to ours. They can learn, remember the past, weigh options, solve problems, flexibly adapt their plans, have individual personalities, and even make difficult, counterintuitive decisions. Lucon-Xiccato interweaves stories from the natural world with personal insights from his own research, offering an engaging overview of what we now know about fish intelligence. Along the way, he shares fresh perspectives on a host of timely issues, such as the ethics of fish farming and the effects of climate change and human influence on our oceans.

Posing tantalizing questions about the evolutionary roots of cognition and awareness, Smart as a Fish reveals that, beneath the surface, the brain of a fish is far more complex than we ever imagined—and perhaps not so different from our own.
books.bio: Tyrone Lucon-Xiccato is associate professor of zoology at the University of Ferrara in Italy and associate editor of the journal Animal Cognition . His work has been featured in Nature Italy , Le Scienze , and on BBC Earth, among other media outlets.

books.title: Starting Over
books.subtitle: A Neuro-Emotional, Cajun, Rock ‘n’ Roll Memoir
books.tagline: How a Cajun boy became one of the world’s leading neuroscientists—and created a musical genre that fused his science with a lifelong passion for music.
books.description:
We are the stories we tell ourselves about ourselves. How these stories unfold, as much by chance as by choice, is key to maintaining our sense of self through life’s disorienting changes. Neuroscientist Joseph LeDoux is no stranger to such changes. In the remarkable life story he tells in Starting Over , his own experiences vividly and intimately illustrate how narratives, both conscious and unconscious, help us navigate the minefields of life.

Coming out of a part of Louisiana called Cajun Country with two degrees in Business from LSU, LeDoux somehow ended up with a PhD in psychology for discoveries he made about the human brain’s conscious experiences. Similar unlikely detours followed, all entailing starting over in a fundamental way. LeDoux describes how he arrived at each: his breakthrough views about emotional consciousness; coping with the death of his young son Jacob; and his graduation from playing in a band of scientists, The Amygdaloids, to writing songs for them, which led to a novel musical genre.

LeDoux came to be known for his ground-breaking research that made the cluster of neurons known as the “amygdala” synonymous with fear but came to believe that the revolution his research helped spawn had gotten the story wrong. This book explains how and why he turned against the tide.
books.bio: Joseph LeDoux is Professor Emeritus at NYU and an elected member of the National Academy of Sciences. He is the recipient of numerous awards and is also the author of many books, including Anxious , which won the APA William James Book Award, The Deep History of Ourselves , and The Four Realms of Existence . His music has been the subject of a play, Map of Your Mind , and was featured in Werner Herzog’s 2024 film Theatre of Thought . A documentary on Amazon, Neuroscience and Emotions , explores his life, work, and music.

books.title: The Analytical Advantage
books.subtitle: A Data-Informed Approach to Strategy Development in Higher Education
books.authors: Henry Zheng and Gail B. Marsh
books.tagline: An analytics-centered approach to higher education strategy that shows leaders how to make data-informed decisions, define strategic positioning, and build sustainable competitive advantage.
books.description:
In today’s higher education environment, universities are facing a rapidly evolving landscape that demands a more nuanced and agile approach to strategy development and implementation. The Analytical Advantage by Henry Zheng and Gail Marsh offers a data-driven approach to strategic planning in higher education, addressing challenges like declining enrollments, budget constraints, and increased competition. The authors focus on data analytics as the principal force for competitive positioning and strategic decision-making. For each section of the book, key data questions and guidelines are provided to facilitate effective strategy discussions and decisions.

The book distinguishes itself through three key features. First, it offers a comprehensive framework to guide institutions through strategy formulation and implementation, focusing on intents and outcomes, identifying competitive positions and strategic trade-offs, and developing strategies to leverage an organization’s core strengths. Second, data analytics are interwoven throughout, demonstrating how qualitative and quantitative data support effective strategy development through the Competitive Arenas of Higher Education model. Finally, drawing on the authors’ experiences as senior strategy leaders, the book provides practical, real-world examples and actionable tools applicable across all university governance levels—from the board of trustees to department chairships.
books.bio:
Henry Zheng (Author)

Henry Zheng is Vice Provost for Institutional Effectiveness and Planning at Carnegie Mellon University, where he serves on the University Leadership Council, Provost’s Leadership Council, University Strategic Planning Committee, and the Student Success Steering Committee. He is the coeditor of Big Data on Campus .

Gail B. Marsh (Author)

Gail B. Marsh is the former Senior Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer for The Ohio State University and The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. She currently serves as a senior management advisor and executive coach to board members, presidents, and senior leaders in higher education and health care.

books.title: The Blockchain Chronicles
books.subtitle: A Social History of Ideology, Code, and Law
books.authors: Primavera De Filippi, Joel Dietz, Morshed Mannan and Kelsie Nabben
books.tagline: A foundational social history of blockchain technology, tracing how cypherpunk ideology, cryptographic code, legal imagination, and financial experimentation gave rise to cryptocurrencies and Web3.
books.description:
The Blockchain Chronicles tells the story of blockchain’s emergence from a fringe crypto-anarchist experiment into a contested infrastructure reshaping money, finance, governance, and society. Primavera De Filippi, Joel Dietz, Morshed Mannan, and Kelsie Nabben chart the journey from early cypherpunk manifestos and cryptographic experiments to the emergence of Bitcoin, Ethereum, decentralized finance, DAOs, and network states.

Combining primary sources with historical, legal, and social analysis, the authors critically examine the ideas and debates that shaped blockchain’s development. The book situates foundational texts, including Satoshi Nakamoto’s Bitcoin white paper and Vitalik Buterin’s early writings on Ethereum, within the broader intellectual traditions of libertarianism, crypto-anarchism, extropian futurism, open-source culture, and decentralized governance.

The book also examines real-world governance crises like the FTX bankruptcy, the Terra/Luna collapse, the DAO hack, and Bitcoin’s scaling wars, providing insight into the many challenges of governing decentralized communities. In doing so, it shows that blockchain is not only a technical architecture, but also a political and legal project: an attempt to redesign trust, authority, ownership, and collective decision-making through code.
books.bio:
Primavera De Filippi (Author)

Primavera De Filippi is Research Director at the National Center of Scientific Research in Paris and Faculty Associate at the Berkman-Klein Center for Internet & Society at Harvard. She is the coauthor of the book Blockchain and the Law and Blockchain Governance (MIT Press). She is the founder and coordinator of the UN Internet Governance Forum’s dynamic coalitions on Blockchain Technology (COALA) and founding member of the Global Future Council on Blockchain Technology at the World Economic Forum.

Joel Dietz (Author)

Joel Dietz is a serial entrepreneur and intellectual historian serving as a Connection Science Fellow at MIT. He authored the first academic work on cryptoeconomics, launched EtherCasts (the earliest smart-contract learning channel), and continues to lecture at leading research institutions globally.

Morshed Mannan (Author)

books.title: The Broken China Dream
books.subtitle: How Reform Revived Totalitarianism
books.tagline: A provocative book that demystifies China’s great democratic leap backward under Xi Jinping, revealing why the country’s embrace of capitalism has given rise to hard authoritarianism, mass surveillance, and one-man rule instead of democracy as many in the West had hoped
books.description:
When China embarked on its transformative journey of modernization in 1979, many believed the country’s turn toward capitalism would put its totalitarian past to rest and mark the birth of a democratic, open society. Instead, China reverted to a neo-totalitarian state, one backed by one of the fastest-growing, most formidable economies on earth. The Broken China Dream pulls back the curtain on the regime of strongman Xi Jinping, revealing why the reforms of the post-Mao era have been reversed on nearly every front—and why the world failed to see it coming.

Exposing the truth behind China’s economic ascendency after the Cultural Revolution, Minxin Pei shows how, following Mao’s death in 1976, Deng Xiaoping strategically deployed the tools of capitalism to preserve the Chinese Communist Party. Deng kept intact the institutional foundations of totalitarianism even as he unleashed private entrepreneurship and courted foreign investment, giving China’s one-party state control of a vast repressive apparatus and the most critical sectors of the economy. Only a fragile balance of power among dueling factions prevented the rise of a totalitarian leader in the two decades after the Tiananmen crackdown in 1989—but this temporary equilibrium collapsed.

Essential to understanding today’s China, this meticulously researched book is a sobering account of why the country’s reformers and institutions could not stop a shrewd and ruthless politician like Xi from resurrecting dormant totalitarian practices that, for the foreseeable future, have spelled the end of the dream of a free and prosperous China.
books.bio: Minxin Pei is the author of several acclaimed books on contemporary China, including The Sentinel State: Surveillance and the Survival of Dictatorship in China , China’s Crony Capitalism: The Dynamics of Regime Decay , and China’s Trapped Transition: The Limits of Developmental Autocracy . He is the Tom and Margot Pritzker ’72 Professor of Government and a George R. Roberts Fellow at Claremont McKenna College.

praise.q: Revealing insights into the current Chinese state, suggesting that it’s less juggernaut than paper tiger.
praise.by: Kirkus Reviews

praise.q: It used to be thought that market-oriented economic reform would lead China in a more liberal direction. In this important book, Pei, a distinguished scholar of Chinese politics, argues that this has proved the opposite of the truth
praise.by: Martin Wolf, Financial Times

praise.q: In this outstanding book, today’s leading analyst of modern China reveals why it has been so easy for Xi Jinping to reinstate a totalitarian system. Minxin Pei shows how an unreformed party-state stood behind the economic miracle and how, in the absence of constraining legal or political institutions, Xi Jinping has found it easy to reimpose rule by fear. Anybody interested in modern China should read this book.
praise.by: Martin Wolf, chief economics commentator at the Financial Times
praise.cred: chief economics commentator at the Financial Times

praise.q: Minxin Pei remains one of the most prescient analysts of modern China’s economic and political development. With The Broken China Dream , he once again offers an indispensable guide to China’s rise—and to the self-imposed weaknesses and contradictions of the path Xi Jinping has chosen.
praise.by: James Fallows, author of China Airborne

praise.q: There are few more prescient China analysts than Minxin Pei. In this book, he provides a clear and lively analysis of how and why China failed to leave authoritarianism behind and instead ended up with a strongman leader intent on challenging the international order. The Broken China Dream offers an excellent primer on the birth and death of China's reform era while sharing unique insights into the future of this rising superpower.”—Ian Johnson, author of Sparks: China’s Underground Historians and Their Battle for the Future and founder of the China Unofficial Archives

Minxin Pei has authored yet another major statement about China’s post-Mao trajectory. His provocative and lucid analysis of China’s political evolution after Tiananmen concludes with a fascinating account of the rise of Xi Jinping. It will focus discussions of China’s recent past and likely futures for some years to come.
praise.by: Andrew G. Walder, Stanford University, author of China Under Mao
praise.cred: Stanford University, author of China Under Mao

books.title: The Celts
books.subtitle: A Modern History
books.tagline: A new history of the Celts that reveals how this once-forgotten people became a pillar of modern national identity in Britain, Ireland, and France
books.description:
Before the Greeks and Romans, the Celts ruled the ancient world. They sacked Rome, invaded Greece, and conquered much of Europe, from Ireland to Turkey. Celts registered deeply on the classical imagination for a thousand years and were variously described by writers like Caesar and Livy as unruly barbarians, fearless warriors, and gracious hosts. But then, in the early Middle Ages, they vanished. In The Celts , Ian Stewart tells the story of their rediscovery during the Renaissance and their transformation over the next few centuries into one of the most popular European ancestral peoples.

The Celts shows how the idea of this ancient people was recovered by scholars, honed by intellectuals, politicians, and other thinkers of various stripes, and adopted by cultural revivalists and activists as they tried to build European nations and nationalisms during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Long-forgotten, the Celts improbably came to be seen as the ancestors of most western Europeans—and as a pillar of modern national identity in Britain, Ireland, and France.

Based on new research conducted across Europe and in the United States, The Celts reveals when and how we came to call much of Europe “Celtic,” why this idea mattered in the past, and why it still matters today, as the tide of nationalism is once again on the rise.
books.bio: Ian Stewart is an intellectual and cultural historian of modern Europe and a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellow at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales in Paris.

praise.q: Vivid . . . Ian Stewart takes an imaginative, scholarly look at Celticism and its shifting interpretations.
praise.by: Linda Colley, Financial Times

praise.q: A capacious survey of the idea of Celticism since the eighteenth century, exploring the contested concepts of race, nationalism, prehistory and cultural revival with scholarly verve and powerfully demonstrating the effect on the present of ideas about the past.
praise.by: Roy Foster, Times Literary Supplement

praise.q: Stewart builds on recent scholarship to make a compelling case for the significance of modern Celticism, in all its paradoxical glory. . . . A big, ambitious, erudite book.
praise.by: Rhys Kaminski-Jones, History Today

praise.q: Breathtaking. . . . The book displays an impressive maturity of judgment, an awe-inspiring panoramic breadth and granular depth of erudition, and a formidable capacity to organise a sprawling range of material.
praise.by: Colin Kidd, Intellectual History Review

praise.q: An iconic people receive a scholar’s attention. . . . Definitive and encyclopedic.
praise.by: Kirkus Reviews

praise.q: Stewart elucidates a clearer understanding of the Celts through disciplines such as linguistics and archaeology.
praise.by: Library Journal

praise.q: [A] sweepingly authoritative study. . . . Readers will embrace so diplomatic an author, and this big, dense book will serve most of those readers not only as the grandest possible report on the current state of Celtic studies but as, one can only hope, a death-knell to the kinds of cheaply sentimental pseudo-histories that usually haunt this subject.
praise.by: Steve Donoghue, Open Letters Review

praise.q: A fine piece of scholarship. . . Stewart’s exposition is clearer than many recent books on the subject and is thoroughly commended.
praise.by: Stewart Rayment, interLib

praise.q: Simultaneously intellectual and (very) readable, The Celts – A Modern History really is. . . . magisterial.
praise.by: David Marx, David Marx Book Reviews

praise.q: [A] radical and definitive study."—David Lorimer, Paradigm Explorer

books.title: The Data Center Next Door
books.subtitle: How Big Tech and AI Are Shaping Our Energy Future
books.tagline: The essential guide to data centers and energy—how Big Tech became a new power on a century-old grid and what's at stake for our neighborhoods. From an internationally recognized legal expert in energy, environmental, and emerging technology law and policy named a “visionary thinker” by Popular Science .
books.description:
From an internationally recognized legal expert in energy, environmental, and emerging technology law and policy named a “visionary thinker” by Popular Science .

As Big Tech pours billions into AI, it has brought data centers out of obscurity onto the front page. The largest facilities, “hyperscalers,” are staggering in size and built at unprecedented speed. Their insatiable appetite for local resources has made headlines, yet the deeper story remains untold: these new neighbors are quietly reshaping our energy landscape.

In The Data Center Next Door , Amy Stein reveals how the real impact lies not within the facility, but beyond its walls, at the source of its electricity. Whether it comes from gas, nuclear, wind, solar, or other energy sources, this choice shapes electricity bills, water supplies, air quality, climate, and the resilience of the grid. Equally important, as we enter the era she calls the Tech Energy Transition, Big Tech has emerged as a transformative energy player, rewiring relationships among utilities, investors, and regulators, disrupting entrenched power dynamics, and forcing regulators to reevaluate how the grid is governed.

This book offers a clear framework for understanding the stakes, weighing the trade-offs, and anticipating the next wave of data center development. Timely and rigorously researched, it reveals what our digital dependency is costing us, and the opportunities to reinvent an antiquated grid.
books.bio: Amy L. Stein is the Cone Wagner Professor of Law at the University of Florida Levin College of Law. For 25 years she has examined how innovations like renewable energy, energy storage, and artificial intelligence strain existing legal frameworks, publishing widely in leading law reviews.

books.title: The Resurrection of Species
books.subtitle: Creating Life in the Era of De-Extinction
books.tagline: A fascinating inside account of how genome engineering is enabling de-extinction—and what the ability to create new creatures means ethically and philosophically. From a scientific advisor to the bioscience company Colossal that brought the dire wolf back from extinction.
books.description:
From a scientific advisor to the bioscience company Colossal that brought the dire wolf back from extinction.

It used to be that only evolution could create a species, refining a femur, a knee joint, a tailbone over eons. But now, when those bones are all that remain of some of evolution’s upsets, human beings have found a way to bring back lost species—and perhaps bring new ones to life.

In Speciespoiesis, the scientists behind this evolutionary revolution recount the steps that led to the first genetically engineered creature brought back from extinction, a dire wolf. Christopher Mason describes how he, with his colleague Matthew MacKay, ushered in a new era of genome design and “de-extinction”: the technological methods, such as novel forms of CRISPR and genome editing, the philosophical debates about ethics and the impact of biotechnology, and the considerations about introducing their resurrected wolf to the world.

Inherent in the science of genetic engineering (and re-engineering) are questions about what such power means, how to wield it, who controls it, and what it portends for the future of life on Earth. Looking at de-extinction in light of these issues—outlining the promise and pitfalls of reshaping the relationship between humanity and life past, present, and future— Speciespoiesis is at once a scientific thriller and an urgent philosophical reflection on, quite literally, the meaning of life.
books.bio: Christopher E. Mason is a geneticist and computational biologist who has been a Principal Investigator and Co-investigator of 11 NASA missions and projects. He is Professor of Genomics, Physiology, and Biophysics at Weill Cornell Medicine and the Director of the WorldQuant Initiative for Quantitative Prediction. He also holds affiliate appointments at the New York Genome Center, Yale Law School, and the Consortium for Space Genetics at Harvard Medical School. He is the author of The Next 500 Years (MIT Press).

books.title: The Wildflower Handbook
books.subtitle: A Celebration of Britain and Ireland’s Floral Diversity
books.tagline: A richly detailed photographic resource on the spectacular flora of Britain and Ireland
books.description:
The Wildflower Handbook is a monumental reference to the vascular plants of Britain and Ireland, covering everything from grasses, sedges, rushes, and other flowering plants to ferns and their allies. The introductory section provides an invaluable overview of the natural history of British and Irish flora and shares insights into plant classification, biology, reproduction and life cycles. The illustrated accounts of plant families and species capture the beauty and diversity of the region’s floral heritage in exquisite detail. This one-of-a-kind handbook engages and inspires botanical enthusiasts of all levels, encouraging people to pursue their floral passion while allowing them to hone their identification skills and submit records of their findings.

Covers 1,905 species of vascular plants found growing in the wild in Britain and Ireland

Features 3,880 stunning photos of species in the field along with cutout images of leaves and plants to aid identification

The fact-filled species accounts come with maps provided by the Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland as well as QR codes linking to additional information online

Provides an incisive overview of British and Irish habitats, discussing their appearance, location, component species, ecological significance, and conservation
books.bio: Paul Sterry is a bestselling wildlife author and photographer whose many books include The Biodiversity Gardener (Princeton), Collins BTO Guide to British Birds and Complete British Wild Flowers . Andrew Cleave is a highly regarded educator and environmentalist whose many books include A Naturalist’s Guide to the Trees of Britain and Northern Europe and Field Guide to Coastal Wildflowers of Britain, Ireland and Northwest Europe (Princeton) and Collins Complete Guide to British Coastal Wildlife (both with Paul Sterry).

books.title: The Will to Adorn
books.subtitle: Black Women and Sartorial Choice after Enslavement
books.tagline: How Black women’s everyday choices in personal adornment tell a story of navigating racial and sexual oppression after Emancipation
books.description:
Even amid the racialized servitude, sexual exploitation, and economic disenfranchisement of the post-Emancipation era in the American South, Black women dared to adorn themselves by styling their hair with combs, wearing necklaces crafted out of glass beads, and dyeing coarse cotton fabric with indigo-berry and sweetgum bark. In The Will to Adorn , Ayana Omilade Flewellen examines the material remains of Black women’s sartorial strategies in these decades and argues that such “small finds” as beads, buttons, hairpins, brooches, and lace bobbins compose a new historical narrative of how Black women and girls navigated a society conditioned to view them solely as commodities.

Flewellen looks at the lives of three Black women of the era through personal belongings. Nancy, an enslaved seamstress, escaped the Hermitage Plantation in Tennessee during the Civil War, taking her bedding and clothing—valuable items at that time. Sarah Williams, among the first Black landowners in Texas, maintained a thriving farmstead with her husband and nine children, leaving behind a story told in shoe button hooks and fragments of leather soles. Finally, Lorena, lost in the documentary record if not for her copper wire name pin, offers an example of defiantly individual personal adornment. These objects and others like them, Flewellen shows, provide rich evidence of who these women were, who they wanted to be, and how they wanted to be seen.
books.bio: Ayana Omilade Flewellen is assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at Stanford University, with an affiliation with Stanford’s Archaeology Center, and cofounder of the Society of Black Archaeologists.

books.title: The World at First Light
books.subtitle: A New History of the Renaissance
books.tagline: A magisterial history of the Renaissance and the birth of the modern world
books.description:
The cultural epoch we know as the Renaissance emerged at a certain time and in a certain place. Why then and not earlier? Why there and not elsewhere? In The World at First Ligh t, historian Bernd Roeck explores the cultural and historical preconditions that enabled the European Renaissance. Roeck shows that the rediscovery of ancient knowledge, including the science of the medieval Arab world, played a critical role in shaping the beginnings of Western modernity. He explains that the Renaissance emerged in a part of Europe where competing states and cities formed relatively open societies. Most of the era’s creative minds—from Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo to Copernicus and Galileo—came from the middle classes. The art of arguing flowered, the basso continuo to intellectual and cultural breakthroughs.

Roeck argues that two revolutions shaped the Renaissance: a media revolution, triggered by Gutenberg’s invention of movable type—which itself was a driving force behind the scientific revolution—and the advent of modern science. He also reports on the dark side of the era—hatred of Jews, witch panic, religious wars, and the atrocities of colonialism. In a series of meditative counterfactuals, Roeck considers other cultural rebirths throughout the first millennium, from the Islamic empire to the Carolingians, examining why the epic developments of the Renaissance took place in the West and not elsewhere. The complicated legacy of the Renaissance, he shows, encompasses the art of critical thinking as learned from the ancients, the emergence of the modern state, and the genesis of democracy.
books.bio: Bernd Roeck has been professor of modern history at the University of Zurich and director of the German Centre for Venetian Studies in Venice. He is the author of Florence 1900: The Quest for Arcadia , Civic Culture and Everyday Life in Early Modern Germany , and other books.
