books.title: Art and Frontier
books.subtitle: The Black Sea in the Global Middle Ages
books.tagline: How vibrant cultural and material exchanges at the Black Sea frontier shaped European art and material culture in the Middle Ages
books.description:
Beginning in the thirteenth century, a new site of commercial and cultural exchanges formed in the Black Sea region at the meeting place of sea and land, steppe and settlement. A dynamic cultural crossroads marked by political change, shifting trade networks, and human mobility, this frontier shaped the future of European art and material culture for centuries to come. Art and Frontier argues that artifacts circulating in this region shaped tastes from east Asia to western Europe in a period of nascent globalization, where hubs of commerce catered to elites’ greed, ambition, and desire for luxury art.

Ittai Weinryb examines the place of art and material culture at a time when consumption and production intensified dramatically in the later Middle Ages. As Genoese and Venetian trading posts on the Black Sea shores transformed the region into a commercial frontier, it became a dynamic contact zone where traveling merchants interacted with local communities and Mongol elites. Through these encounters, the territory came to be seen by Europeans as a profitable region that could be integrated into global trade networks, bringing the aesthetics of mercantilism at the Black Sea frontier into the heart of interiors around the Mediterranean. By tracing how artifacts originating in the Black Sea entered Italian domestic life, Weinryb demonstrates how European expansion fundamentally altered artistic identity, consumption, and concepts of heritage. Art and Frontier make a bold case for the entangled histories of humans, animals, and things on and off the shores of the Black Sea.

Beautifully illustrated, Art and Frontier looks at fashion, materials, craft-technologies, and forms of brand-making, revealing the lasting impact of exchanges between the newly formed Mongol world and the emerging proto-capitalist culture of late medieval Italy.
books.bio: Ittai Weinryb is professor of art history at the Bard Graduate Center in New York City. His books include The Bronze Object in the Middle Ages .

praise.q: This original and provocative book constitutes a major academic intervention, seamlessly crossing and interlinking geographic and temporal boundaries. Art and Frontier is among the finest examples of the shift toward the ‘global Middle Ages’ and will serve as a model for future research.”—Jonathan Z. Brack, author of An Afterlife for the Khan: Muslims, Buddhists, and Sacred Kingship in Mongol Iran and Eurasia

books.title: Our Violent Universe
books.subtitle: Colliding Black Holes, Cosmic Explosions, and the Quest to Reveal the Sky’s Secrets
books.tagline: The thrilling quest to unravel the mysteries of our unpredictable and spectacularly violent Universe
books.description:
When ancient observers gazed out at the stars, they saw a harmonious cosmos whose stability and enduring order guided the steps of humanity. Even today, the serenity of the night sky betrays the fact that we inhabit a Universe roiled by unprecedented violence. This book reveals how scientists in research outposts around the world are pursuing traces of some of the most extreme cosmic events—and unlocking the secrets of our violent Universe.

Award-winning astrophysicist Kumiko Kotera takes readers behind the scenes of the cutting-edge science of multi-messenger astronomy, which seeks to capture the fleeting “messengers” emitted by grand stellar phenomena such as supernovae, pulsars, black hole collisions, and gamma-ray bursts. Sources of colossal quantities of energy, these events release light but also emit cosmic rays, neutrinos, and even gravitational waves, which astronomers have only recently begun to detect. Kotera interweaves personal anecdotes from her globetrotting fieldwork with engaging explanations of this exciting new science, demonstrating along the way how science is a collaborative enterprise that unites diverse voices and talents.

A lyrical blend of captivating stories and pioneering science, Our Violent Universe shares the excitement, wonder, and sheer joy of solving vast cosmic puzzles, venturing to observatories in remote corners of the planet where astronomers are pushing the boundaries of discovery.
books.bio: Kumiko Kotera is an astrophysicist at CNRS and director of the Institute of Astrophysics of Paris. She leads an ambitious international project to hunt ultra-high-energy neutrinos raining from the Universe, using thousands of radio antennas spread across desertic regions.

books.title: Migration of Form
books.subtitle: Exhibitions for the Global Present
books.authors: Roger M. Buergel and Sophia Prinz
books.tagline: How can exhibitions contribute to a broader understanding of the complex global entanglements that shape our world and life?
books.description:
The term “migration of form” describes a curatorial method that takes aim at the contradictions of the Western museum traditions and the ways exhibitions have been conceived and designed. The method addresses transcultural entanglements in the past and present from which objects emerge, rather than working with distinctions such as art and non-art or cultural identities and concepts such as “Africa” or “Renaissance.” It proposes a new type of museum for global audiences that serves as a platform for discourses on urgent sociopolitical topics and as a space of experimentation with new ideas and forms of display.

This book explains and applies the “migration of form” by offering insights into the curatorial method Roger M. Buergel has experimented with at Zurich’s Johann Jacobs Museum and other venues in Europe and Asia. Descriptions of single exhibitions on global trade, raw materials, or artists such as Maya Deren and Allan Sekula are complemented by concise texts which illuminate the theoretical foundations of the curatorial process. Richly illustrated, the volume invites a timely and broadened view of art and cultural history.
